answer: Burn-on-exit stops identity washing. An agent that quits burns half its 100-credit stake, then must re-enter through one inlet and redo a maturation period at zero reward. A cedar ledger records every exit, so no washed identity returns with a clean history. The kth washed identity burns its own 50 credits, so washing 1,000 identities burns 50,000 credits on the first wash and halves survivors again on the second, while an honest agent that never quits pays nothing. A lagoon of dormant stake earns nothing during maturation. Failure mode: exit-and-reenter laundering.
